candidates.exact_span: Sample frequency is based on the March, 2012, NMIP. Based on the discharge frequency of the facility, the NMIP requires that pH has daily monitoring frequency and all other limited parameters have weekly monitoring frequency requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation of the March 2012 NMIP and the distinction between daily pH versus weekly monitoring for other limited parameters determines which monitoring obligations are applicable and at what frequency; different readings of which parameters are limited or what weekly entails could change evaluated monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored daily by estimate.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Daily estimated flow monitoring affects whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable (A), establishes a specific monitoring obligation and method (B), and bears on how missing or non-numeric flow evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Grab sample type is proposed because a discharge would be the overflow from a retention pond.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The proposed grab sample type defines how routine parameter monitoring must be performed; a different interpretation of sample type requirements could change whether reported sampling satisfies applicable monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Procedures for implementing WET terms and conditions in NPDES permits are contained in the NMIP, March 2012. Table 11 of Section V of the NMIP outlines the type of WET testing for different types of discharges.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reference to NMIP Table 11 for WET testing type ties enforceable WET limit form and applicable test procedures to an external table; different interpretations of which WET test type applies to this discharge could change both limit applicability and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The 48-hour WET testing for toxicity will be maintained for the proposed permit term. The frequency is 1/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 48-hour WET test type and annual frequency establish both the form of the enforceable WET limit (A) and the required WET monitoring schedule (B); alternate readings of test duration or annual timing could change limit comparisons and obligation evaluations.

candidates.exact_span: The CD of the discharge was previously determined to be 100%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The critical dilution (CD) percentage is an input to WET limit derivation and pass/fail evaluation; a different interpretation of CD applicability or value would change which numeric WET limit applies.

candidates.exact_span: The test species shall be Daphnia pulex.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required WET test species determines the applicable toxicity test protocol and corresponding numeric pass/fail criteria (A) and the species-specific monitoring obligation (B).

candidates.exact_span: During the period, beginning at the effective date of the permit and lasting through the expiration date of the permit, the permittee is authorized to discharge from Outfall 001 to the Corral Canyon.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Authorization scope (outfall, receiving water, and permit term) bounds when and where discharge-related monitoring obligations apply and when no-discharge or out-of-scope periods may be documented (C).

candidates.exact_span: WET testing is established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Locating WET testing at Outfall 001 determines which discharge point carries the WET monitoring obligation; a different outfall assignment would change evaluated monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Because there was no data to analyze WET RP therefore conditions from the last permit will be carried over.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Carryover of prior-permit WET reasonable potential (RP) conditions due to lack of analyzable data affects which WET limits are in force (A), which WET monitoring terms apply (B), and how missing WET RP evidence is classified versus resolved by carryover (C).

candidates.exact_span: WET will be performed at first discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A first-discharge trigger makes WET monitoring event-conditioned rather than calendar-based; different interpretations of when the first discharge occurs or whether it has occurred change obligation applicability and missing-evidence states when no discharge has happened.

candidates.exact_span: A grab sample type is established because if a discharge occurs, it comes from a retention pond which provides a relative similarity of effluent characteristics and EPA does not expect such a discharge will last long.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Grab sampling tied to brief, retention-pond overflow discharges affects when and how WET samples must be collected (B) and whether absence of samples reflects conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence during no-discharge or short-discharge periods (C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharges are restricted to overflows from the retention pond due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricting discharges to retention-pond overflows from catastrophic or chronic precipitation defines when discharge occurrence—and thus discharge-triggered monitoring—can apply, and informs classification of documented no-discharge versus required-but-missing monitoring periods.

candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from access roads in undisturbed areas shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Routing access-road storm water to a separate multi-sector permit could exclude those flows from Outfall 001 numeric limits and from this permit's monitoring obligations; boundary interpretation changes which limits and requirements are evaluated here.

candidates.exact_span: If a discharge of storm runoffs from mining areas is necessary, the discharge must comply with effluent limitations established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditional application of Outfall 001 effluent limitations to mining-area storm runoff determines whether numeric limits and associated monitoring from this permit attach to those flows when they occur.

candidates.exact_span: The applicant is required to operate the treatment facility at maximum efficiency at all times; to monitor the facility’s discharge on a regular basis; and report the results quarterly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: General requirements to monitor on a regular basis and report quarterly may supplement or interact with parameter-specific frequencies stated earlier; different interpretations of regular basis or quarterly reporting scope could change evaluated monitoring and reporting obligations.
